These are the classical functions that are the functions, let's say, of the ministries, line ministries in the republic of Slovenia. So obviously, the central government authority and the presidency of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina could not out of besieged Sarajevo control what is happening in the local communities; and thus, they have asked by this decree for establishment of seven districts and for those districts to really run economy on their own area. And the way I see, what were economic developments in areas with Croat majority over the 1991 to 1994 period, especially after, you know, second half of 1992 and 1993, these were very similar developments, very much in line with the authority vested in district by the presidency decree with a power of law on establishment and work of districts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Your Honour, I don't know how much time I have left, but I do want to wrap it up, if I can. Five minutes? All right. Unless there are any questions --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Karnavas, the Registrar informs that you have five minutes left.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Unless there are any questions concerning this area, I will move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Just returning to the question of the districts. When on Monday you mentioned this point, I asked myself what was the purpose of addressing this question, and now in seeing the text before our eyes and particularly line 6 where we mention the district of Mostar, et cetera, I'm drawing a parallel with the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, and I'm asking myself, and you may well be able to enlighten me here, as to whether in fact the district that was envisaged in Sarajevo in this text is not in fact give or take what we have with the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. What are your thoughts on that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, you are correct. The district of Mostar was centred in Mostar, and the territories municipalities as they are mentioned here, they are more or less those that compose the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, and presidency established in this district is actually giving the District Secretariat for Economy authority to manage the economy in this very area and, also, request other function -- there are, you know, other -- this economy -- this secretariat for economy, social affairs, finance, education, et cetera, all to do measures which we have seen that were undertaken by the Croatian Defence Council of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. It was just not titled district of Mostar or whatever it would be. I have analysed their economic powers vested in them. I was not looking from the point of view of which local communities were, but clearly, central government authority realised that instead of having 50-plus small local communities doing what they were asked to do with this law on the financing of the social needs in the time of the war, realised the need to coordinate and to have an organisation between the republic and local communities, and they called them district. The way I see economically Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, I see it as this intermediate level. That later on merged into Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You have a question? Okay. I thought I saw you on the ready.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. I have five minutes left, and we have two slides left, 37 and 38, and basically these concern your final remarks concerning your presentation, which is a summary essentially of your report, 200-page-plus report, with nearly a thousand footnotes. If you could kindly wrap it up for us.

utterances.speaker: MILAN CVIKL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in these two slides are my final remarks. With the war, the provision of administrative social services was severely disrupted. There was a vacuum created. Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina did not have an effective governance. Local communities and regional authorities had not much choice but to react to this situation. To enable survival of the people to ensure appropriate supply and demands, they have acted as one state should act in war circumstances. And what then emerges, as I was asked to look deeply into what was happening in the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, is that the Croatian Defence Council seriously attempt to resolve the basic needs and services at the local and the regional level. It could wait. It could do nothing. It could not re-establish the border crossing with the Republic of Croatia. It could not relicense Hrvatska banka or insurance company, but if they would not do nothing then it would simply mean that the region would connect to Croatia. They acted differently. They acted so that they were solving the basic economic and social needs of the population. And on the last slide, I say that these regional actions were somehow based or they were a follow-up on the local actions, and I have shown and was comparing the matters of the local communities; I have seen no difference. Local communities and later regional authorities acted in a very similar manner. Tuzla, Jablanica, Maglaj have same problem. And yes, Bosnia-Herzegovina suffered an economic collapse with the war. If that would happen in Slovenia and Slovenia would have one-year war, we would most likely have such economic area being created. I hope that my study and what we have been -- what we have been presented is that you, High Court, got a good review of what happened on economic front in the country. What needed to be done by local authorities and later by regional authorities to ensure social and other services and functions to be performed for the citizens was a logical reactions once the federal and republican institution ceased to fulfill their economic functions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Cvikl. With that answer, I have no more questions on direct examination. I appreciate your testimony. I would hope that you would be as frank and forthright with the Prosecution or anyone else who may have any other questions for you during the next couple of days.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honours, that concludes my direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Karnavas. I have just a very brief follow-up question, but taking advantage of your -- the fact that you're Slovenian to put this question to you. Earlier, I by chance looked at the map of your country because the Registrar maybe just mishandled and in fact, your -- the map of your country appeared on the screen. I noted that an important country bordered on your frontier Austria, so if I'm mistaken don't hesitate to interrupt me. So Austria shares the border with you now. At the time of the dismantling of the former Yugoslavia and when your country acceded to independence, I assume that Austria through its economic renown no doubt played some role in the regions close to its border, but Slovenian regions. To your knowledge, in those years, 1991, 1992, was there not in circulation Austrian currency as there were Deutschemarks in Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but as far as the Austrian currency is concerned, you should know that since early '60s, there's a fixed exchange between Deutschmark and shilling that is 7:1, and since most of the gastarbeiters were using -- were actually in Germany, Deutschemark was more prevailed para-currency in territory either of Slovenia as well as Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. Simply more gastarbeiters were there, but I believe if anyone would bring a shilling, since there is a fixed exchange 7:1, they would also take shillings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So if I understand well, in the areas, in the border areas there circulated in the years 1991, 1992, it appears in addition to your own currency, there were Deutschemarks and Austrian shillings in circulation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. In Slovenia, immediately after the independence on the 25th of June, we only established custom borders. Then there was a two-weeks attacks by the Yugoslav Army. Then there was a peace, and with this peace agreement, we have agreed that for three months we will not undertake follow-up measures. So only on 8 of October 1991, three months after the signing of the Brioni agreement, which was on 8th of July, we replaced Yugoslav dinars with the Slovene coupons. In the meantime, there were parallel currency, people were using different type of cash, including, you know, shillings, Deutschemark, dollars, et cetera. Once on 8 of October 1991, Yugoslav dinar was out of the system and there were Slovene coupons we were doing our utmost to reduce the inflation and to increase the backing of the Slovene coupons. As we were also having up and running banking system and up and running Social Accounting Office in Slovenia in 1992 to 1994, there was no need to continuation of people using either on the black market or as a parallel currency at the border crossing also Deutschemark or shillings. So down the line Slovene dollar, as it was later renowned and stamped, et cetera, became a strong convertible currency, and that lasted up to 1st of January 2007 when it replaced dollars with Euro. So the situation was we were not in war situation and we had a strong currency because if you would look at the time in our budget you would see that there were no financing of the central government budget from the central bank, and thus currency which was utilized was trustworthy currency. 24 25

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. But the shift to the Slovenian tolar, which you said was a strong, hard currency, that happened gradually. The Slovenian inhabitants, did they have fears or doubts, and at that point did they prefer world-recognised Deutschemarks and convertible, I mean, didn't that all take some time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, that has to do with two factors. First, on 8th of October when we put in replacement the new coupons, we also have established exchange rate which was a fluctuating exchange rate, which means we did not try to attempt and steal from citizens holding Slovene dollar some value to so-called inflation tax. So, yes, it took some time but the most important for Slovene independence and economic development was that our monetary and our fiscal policy were prudent. We did not need to, it's true, have a lot of expenditure on defence, but we did not have holes in our budgets so people, you know, trusted Slovene tolar. Actually, in 1990s, bank of Slovenia and Slovene tolar are among the most valued institutions in Slovenia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very good. I put that question, you have understood it was to establish a link with the circulation of the Deutschemark in Herzegovina at that time to see whether there were points of convergence or divergence. Thank you for answering my question. Mr. Kovacic, have you been able to agree with Mr. Praljak to put questions, if you have any?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, with your permission, I have made an agreement with Mr. Kovacic and I might need 15 minutes in actual fact to ask the witness a few questions, and I'll tell you what I'm going to refer to. Unfortunately, I can't do that this evening. I can't start this evening, but it was on page 81 with your question that this came to mind, which -- your question relating to a document on our screens. At that point in time on our screens we had a document which was a financial report of the HZ HB, and you asked the question, you asked whether it was that amount because the rest was financed by the municipalities. Now, the witness's answer followed, and I think there might have been a misunderstanding rather than an imprecision because the witness gave different conclusions in his report. So I should just like to show the witness some documents, to put them to him, which he saw during the preparation. This would last 15 to 20 minutes, but if possible I would like to start tomorrow morning once I prepared the documents. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very good, we are close to 7 o'clock.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, let me respond to your question. No, I have not had consultations with Mr. Praljak and reached an agreement, but with your permission may I have five minutes perhaps tomorrow morning, it's not a good idea to do that this evening, but anyway I have your decision of the 24th of April here before me, your decision of June and September, as well, and the Appeals Chamber's decision dated September 2008, and I consider that my request was completely in keeping with the decision of the 24th of April, which is in force, and I, therefore, request that you give me five minutes before we introduce the witness tomorrow to make a submission, bearing in mind your ruling and referring exclusively to your ruling, your decision. And I'd just like to remind you so that you can have a look at this yourself. On the 24th of April was the date of your ruling, which set the frameworks and certain limitations for cross-examination by the accused. Afterwards, there were certain problems with the interpretation of that ruling and in June last year you made a new ruling which you narrowed down and gave a restrictive interpretation with respect to a particular and special circumstances. And we appealed that ruling, and after the Appeals Chamber's ruling, the only decision in force is your ruling of the 24th of April. And that particular ruling, I don't want to present my arguments about that now, we can go into that tomorrow, but anyway, it provides for two specific circumstances, when in principle you will allow the accused to ask questions himself. In that ruling, at paragraph 3, you provided for the following, and I'm going to read it out: [In English] "Exceptional circumstances relate in particular to the examination of events in which an accused participated personally or the examination of the issues about which he possess specific expertise."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacic, Mr. Kovacic, you have misquoted because you have omitted, and you always omit, the term "exceptionally," and I would suggest that you reflect on the term "exceptionally" in this context before you address us tomorrow. It seems that you are already repeating your arguments now. Maybe you do that tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Judge Trechsel, I'm not sure there is a misunderstanding in the interpretation, but I read it out word by word, the penultimate sentence of paragraph 3 of your own ruling of April 24th, and it reads as follows: As I said in the previous sentence that the accused can ask questions when there are exceptional circumstances, and in this sentence you go on to explain what those exceptional circumstances are, and those are the two situations, either about events in which the accused took part personally, or has specific expertise. And I feel, Judge Trechsel, that you are talking about the decision of June, you went a step further, where you restricted -- you gave a restricted interpretation, and that decision was rescinded by the Appeals Chamber decision, but I suggest that you look at the third paragraph of the 24th of April decision and I'd like to repeat my submission tomorrow and explain why Mr. Praljak wants to cross-examine, otherwise we'll go back to where we were in June. You're interpreting your own decision in a different way. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, in the timetable -- I'll give you the floor, Mr. Stringer -- tomorrow, five minutes for Mr. Kovacic, and 15 minutes for Ms. Nozica. Mr. Stringer, what would you like to say?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Just to simply note that so far the Prosecution has not taken a position or expressed a position on regards to Mr. Praljak's request. If there are going to be submissions tomorrow, we will be prepared to make our own submissions at that time. We are strongly of the view that in this particular situation the applicable decision of the Trial Chamber and Appeals Chamber, which of course is still in effect, is not nearly met in respect of this witness. And we will be prepared to make additional submissions tomorrow should the Trial Chamber wish to entertain this yet again, despite my understanding that it had in fact already ruled. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. President, if -- I just wish to inform the Trial Chamber that Mr. Cvikl is an extremely busy man. We are very grateful that he was able to come here and devote a week essentially. He will not be able to stay beyond Thursday, and it would be highly inconvenient, and in fact unfair, to have to bring him back because we are having these procedural disputes. So I would ask that that be taken into consideration. If special hearings need to be held, they should be convened, but Mr. Cvikl should be allowed to finish his testimony and go back to his work and to the government of Slovenia who depends on him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Witness, rest assured there will be 15 minutes for Ms. Nozica, after which Mr. Kovacic will speak for five minutes, the Chamber will take a decision. Even if there's a positive ruling, it won't take hours, and the Prosecution will have four hours for the cross-examination. So we will end Thursday and you won't have to return, save events beyond our control such as a fire as happened not so long ago where we had to evacuate the premises, or that the Judge was struck simultaneously with a heart attack, but those are pretty remote, extreme assumptions that I'm just mentioning. So we will meet again tomorrow at 14.15. Thank you.
